body.statement: For every \(\kappa\in K\), the Cartesian formulas define Borel score laws with support \(D\). With \(c_m=2^{-(\bar\kappa-2)-5}\), \(C_m=2^{\bar\kappa-2}+1\), \(c_J=1\), and \(C_{\mathrm{iso}}=5+4\cdot8^{1/\epsilon}\), \(P^{0,\mathrm{iso}}\in\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa\) and \(P^{0,\mathrm{perv}}\in\mathrm{Perv}_\kappa\). For every \(x=(0,s_0)\in B\) and \(0<h\leq h_0\), \(2^{-\alpha-3}h^\kappa\leq q_t^{\mathrm{perv}}(x,h)\leq h^\kappa/2\), \(q_t^{\mathrm{iso}}(x,h)\geq2^{-\alpha-5}h^\kappa\), and \(q_t^{\mathrm{iso}}(x,h)\leq2^\alpha h^2(|s_0|+h)^\alpha\); when \(|s_0|\geq2h\), also \(q_t^{\mathrm{iso}}(x,h)\geq2^{-\alpha-3}h^2|s_0|^\alpha\). At the origin, \(q_t^{\mathrm{iso}}(0,h)=D_\alpha h^\kappa\), and the isolated packing envelope holds for every admissible \(u\), including \(u=1\). Every tent law is a Borel causal law in the same profile class, obeys consistency, has \(L\)-Lipschitz means, and separates \(\tau_P\) from the baseline by \(Lh/2\) at its active center. The squared-tent identities are \(\int_D\psi_{j,h}^2f_{\mathrm{perv},\alpha}=Q_{\mathrm{perv},\alpha}h^\kappa\) and \(\int_D\psi_{0,h}^2f_{\mathrm{iso},\alpha}=Q_{\mathrm{iso},\alpha}h^\kappa\). Hence \(\mathrm{KL}((P^{j,h,\mathrm{perv}}_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},(P^{0,\mathrm{perv}}_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n})=nL^2Q_{\mathrm{perv},\alpha}h^{\kappa+2}/(32\sigma^2)\), with the isolated coefficients at the centered site. Constants are uniform over \(K\). At \(\kappa=3\), \(Q_{\mathrm{perv},1}=1/15\) and the divergence is \(nL^2h^5/(480\sigma^2)\).
body.justification: This attributed supporting proposition gives normalized Borel flat score laws, exact one-sided masses, full isolated and pervasive profile membership, valid causal Gaussian tents, and exact product divergence.
body.gap: No separate novelty is claimed for the witness; it replaces the banked parent's circular geometry with a directly audited flat construction on the present target segment.
body.consumer: It supplies the same-class two-point and multiple-testing experiments for \(\mathrm{thm:exact\text{-}endpoint\text{-}minimax\text{-}lower\text{-}bounds}\).
body.proof_tex:
Put \(A=\bar\kappa-2\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:exponent\text{-}window}\),
\[
 \epsilon\leq \alpha=\kappa-2\leq A.
 \tag{1}
\]
We first verify normalization and support.  Cartesian integration gives
\[
 \int_D \frac{\alpha+1}{4}|r|^\alpha\,dr\,ds
 =\frac{\alpha+1}{4}\frac{2}{\alpha+1}\,2=1.
 \tag{2}
\]
By the vertical-slice definition, \(V_{\mathrm{disk}}\) is the Lebesgue
area of the unit disk.  For \(0\leq\rho\leq1\),
\(1-\rho^\alpha=\int_\rho^1\alpha t^{\alpha-1}\,dt\).  Integrating this
nonnegative identity first over the disk and then over its nonnegative layer
parameter, and using the quadratic scaling of planar Lebesgue measure, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
4-Z_\alpha
 &=\int_{\{z:\|z\|_2\leq1\}}(1-\|z\|_2^\alpha)\,dz\\
 &=\int_0^1\alpha t^{\alpha-1}
      \operatorname{Leb}\{z:\|z\|_2\leq t\}\,dt\\
 &=V_{\mathrm{disk}}\int_0^1\alpha t^{\alpha+1}\,dt
 =V_{\mathrm{disk}}\frac{\alpha}{\alpha+2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
This proves the asserted normalizer.  The integrand defining \(Z_\alpha\)
is at most one.  On the set \(\{(r,s)\in D:|r|\geq1/2\}\), which has area
two, it is at least \(2^{-\alpha}\).  Hence
\[
 2^{1-\alpha}\leq Z_\alpha\leq4.
 \tag{4}
\]
Thus both formulas in \(\mathrm{def:flat\text{-}densities}\) are
nonnegative Borel densities of integral one.  The pervasive density is
positive off the line \(r=0\), and the isolated density is positive off the
origin.  Every nonempty relatively open subset of \(D\) contains a
positive-area subset avoiding the respective null set, so every such open
set has positive mass.  Both score laws consequently have support exactly
\(D\).

Fix \(x=(0,s_0)\in B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<h\leq h_0\).  Since
\(|s_0|\leq1/2\) and \(h_0\leq1/8\), the closed radius-\(h\) ball about
\(x\) lies in \(D\), including when \(s_0=\pm1/2\).  Its points have norm
at most \(|s_0|+h\leq5/8\), so the clipping in the isolated density is
inactive there.  Reflection in \(r=0\) shows that the two one-sided masses
are equal; the different convention on the line itself is immaterial by
absolute continuity.

For the pervasive density, vertical Cartesian slices yield
\[
 q_t^{\mathrm{perv}}(x,h)
 =\frac{\alpha+1}{2}\int_0^h r^\alpha\sqrt{h^2-r^2}\,dr
 =C_\alpha h^{\alpha+2}=C_\alpha h^\kappa.
 \tag{5}
\]
The relevant half-ball contains the rectangle
\(0\leq|r|\leq h/2\), \(|s-s_0|\leq h/2\), and is contained in the
rectangle \(0\leq|r|\leq h\), \(|s-s_0|\leq h\).  Both rectangles remain
in \(D\) at the endpoints of \(B\).  Integrating over them gives
\[
 \frac{\alpha+1}{4}h\int_0^{h/2}r^\alpha\,dr
 =2^{-\alpha-3}h^\kappa
 \leq q_t^{\mathrm{perv}}(x,h)
 \leq \frac{\alpha+1}{4}(2h)\int_0^h r^\alpha\,dr
 =\frac12h^\kappa.
 \tag{6}
\]

For the isolated density, use on the relevant side the rectangle
\(h/2\leq|r|\leq3h/4\), \(|s-s_0|\leq h/4\).  It has area \(h^2/8\),
lies in the radius-\(h\) ball because
\((3/4)^2+(1/4)^2<1\), and has \(\|z\|_2\geq h/2\).  Equation (4) gives
\[
 q_t^{\mathrm{iso}}(x,h)
 \geq \frac1{Z_\alpha}\frac{h^2}{8}\left(\frac h2\right)^\alpha
 \geq2^{-\alpha-5}h^\kappa.
 \tag{7}
\]
Conversely, the half-ball has area at most \(2h^2\), and
\(\|z\|_2\leq|s_0|+h\) there.  The lower bound on \(Z_\alpha\) in (4)
therefore implies
\[
 q_t^{\mathrm{iso}}(x,h)
 \leq2^{\alpha-1}\,2h^2(|s_0|+h)^\alpha
 =2^\alpha h^2(|s_0|+h)^\alpha.
 \tag{8}
\]
If \(|s_0|\geq2h\), the rectangle
\(0\leq|r|\leq h/2\), \(|s-s_0|\leq h/2\) is inside the half-ball, has
area \(h^2/2\), and satisfies
\(\|z\|_2\geq|s_0|-h/2\geq|s_0|/2\).  Using \(Z_\alpha\leq4\),
\[
 q_t^{\mathrm{iso}}(x,h)
 \geq\frac14\frac{h^2}{2}
       \left(\frac{|s_0|}{2}\right)^\alpha
 =2^{-\alpha-3}h^2|s_0|^\alpha.
 \tag{9}
\]

At the origin, the same nonnegative layer calculation as in (3) gives
\[
 \int_{\{\|z\|_2\leq1\}}\|z\|_2^\alpha\,dz
 =V_{\mathrm{disk}}-
   V_{\mathrm{disk}}\frac{\alpha}{\alpha+2}
 =\frac{2V_{\mathrm{disk}}}{\alpha+2}.
\]
Scaling by \(h\), taking one half by reflection, and dividing by
\(Z_\alpha\) yield
\[
 q_t^{\mathrm{iso}}(0,h)
 =\frac{V_{\mathrm{disk}}}{(\alpha+2)Z_\alpha}h^{\alpha+2}
 =D_\alpha h^\kappa.
 \tag{10}
\]

We next verify every profile condition.  By (1), (6), and (7), both score
laws obey
\[
 q_t(x,h)\geq2^{-A-5}h^\kappa=c_mh^\kappa.
 \tag{11}
\]
For the pervasive law, (6) and \(C_m=2^A+1>1/2\) show that every site of
\(B\) is thin at level \(C_mh^\kappa\).  The points
\(s_j=-1/2+jh\), \(0\leq j\leq\lfloor1/h\rfloor\), are \(h\)-separated,
and an \(h\)-separated subset of an interval of length one has at most
\(\lfloor1/h\rfloor+1\) points.  Hence
\[
 J_{P^{0,\mathrm{perv}}}(h,C_mh^\kappa)
 =\lfloor1/h\rfloor+1\geq h^{-1}=c_Jh^{-1}.
 \tag{12}
\]
For the isolated law, (8) at \(s_0=0\) gives
\(q_t^{\mathrm{iso}}(0,h)\leq2^\alpha h^\kappa<C_mh^\kappa\), so the
origin is a thin site for every admitted \(h\).

For the full isolated envelope, suppose
\(a_{P^{0,\mathrm{iso}}}((0,s_0),h)\leq u\).  The side masses are equal.
By (9), either \(|s_0|<2h\), or
\[
 |s_0|\leq2\,8^{1/\alpha}
 \left(\frac{u}{h^2}\right)^{1/\alpha}.
 \tag{13}
\]
Thus the thin set is contained in a centered interval of radius
\[
 R=2h+2\,8^{1/\alpha}
 \left(\frac{u}{h^2}\right)^{1/\alpha}.
\]
An \(h\)-separated subset of an interval of radius \(R\) has at most
\(1+2R/h\) elements.  Since \(\alpha\geq\epsilon\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 J_{P^{0,\mathrm{iso}}}(h,u)
 &\leq5+4\,8^{1/\alpha}h^{-1}
       \left(\frac{u}{h^2}\right)^{1/\alpha}\\
 &\leq\left(5+4\cdot8^{1/\epsilon}\right)
 \left\{1+h^{-1}
       \left(\frac{u}{h^2}\right)^{1/\alpha}\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]
This was derived for every \(u\geq0\), so it applies throughout the
required interval \(C_mh^\kappa\leq u\leq1\), including \(u=1\).
Equations (11)--(14) and the class definitions prove all score-profile
membership assertions.

We now construct the full-data laws and their conditional kernels.  For each
score density, take the product of its Borel probability measure with two
standard Gaussian measures.  Let \(X,Z_0,Z_1\) be the coordinate maps, and
apply the Borel formulas in \(\mathrm{def:gaussian\text{-}tents}\) to define
\(T,Y(0),Y(1),Y\).  Pushforward by these Borel maps gives a Borel full-data
law.  Sharp assignment and consistency hold pointwise.  The regular
conditional law of \((Y(0),Y(1))\) given \(X=z\) is the product of the two
Gaussian kernels with the displayed Borel means, so all conditional means
below are legitimate Borel representatives.

Under a baseline law, \(m_{0,P}=m_{1,P}=0\).  Under a tent law,
\[
 m_{1,P}(z)=a_{\mathrm{tent}}\psi_{j,h}(z),
 \qquad
 m_{0,P}(z)=-a_{\mathrm{tent}}\psi_{j,h}(z).
 \tag{15}
\]
The distance map and positive-part map are one-Lipschitz, so
\(\psi_{j,h}\) is \(h^{-1}\)-Lipschitz.  Since
\(a_{\mathrm{tent}}=Lh/4\), each mean in (15) is \(L/4\)-Lipschitz and
therefore \(L\)-Lipschitz on the required neighborhood.  Its boundary
trace is bounded by
\(a_{\mathrm{tent}}\leq Lh_0/4\leq L/32<L\).  Conditional on \((X,T)\),
the centered observed error is
\(\sigma\{TZ_1+(1-T)Z_0\}\); independence gives, for every
\(\lambda\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 E\!\left[
 e^{\lambda\sigma\{TZ_1+(1-T)Z_0\}}\mid X,T\right]
 =e^{\sigma^2\lambda^2/2}.
 \tag{16}
\]
Thus all baseline and tent laws obey the required smoothness, envelope, and
conditional sub-Gaussian conditions.  A tent changes no score marginal, so
(11)--(14) put every tent law in the same profile class as its baseline.
At the active center \(x_j\), (15) gives
\[
 \|\tau_{P^{j,h}}-\tau_{P^0}\|_\infty
 \geq\tau_{P^{j,h}}(x_j)-\tau_{P^0}(x_j)
 =2a_{\mathrm{tent}}=Lh/2.
 \tag{17}
\]

It remains to calculate the exact information coefficients.  Put
\(d(z)=\|z-x_j\|_2\).  From (5), for \(0\leq t\leq h\), the pervasive
score law satisfies
\[
 P^{0,\mathrm{perv}}\{d(X)\leq t\}=2C_\alpha t^\kappa.
\]
The layer identity
\[
 (1-d/h)_+^2=\int_d^h\frac2h(1-t/h)\,dt
\]
is interpreted as zero when \(d>h\).  Integrating this nonnegative layer
identity against the score law and using the preceding ball probability gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \int_D\psi_{j,h}^2f_{\mathrm{perv},\alpha}
 &=\int_0^h\frac2h(1-t/h)\,2C_\alpha t^\kappa\,dt\\
 &=\frac{4C_\alpha}{(\kappa+1)(\kappa+2)}h^\kappa
 =Q_{\mathrm{perv},\alpha}h^\kappa,
\end{aligned}
\tag{18}
\]
because \(\kappa+1=\alpha+3\) and
\(\kappa+2=\alpha+4\).  At the centered isolated site, (10) gives
\(P^{0,\mathrm{iso}}\{\|X\|_2\leq t\}=2D_\alpha t^\kappa\), and the same
calculation yields
\[
 \int_D\psi_{0,h}^2f_{\mathrm{iso},\alpha}
 =Q_{\mathrm{iso},\alpha}h^\kappa.
 \tag{19}
\]

Under a tent law, the conditional observed mean relative to the baseline is
\(\mu_j(X,T)=(2T-1)a_{\mathrm{tent}}\psi_{j,h}(X)\).  Direct integration
of two Gaussian densities with common variance \(\sigma^2\) gives
conditional divergence \(\mu_j(X,T)^2/(2\sigma^2)\).  The score and
treatment laws are the same under the baseline and alternative.  Hence (18)
and \(a_{\mathrm{tent}}^2=L^2h^2/16\) imply
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P^{j,h,\mathrm{perv}}_{\mathrm{obs}},
                    P^{0,\mathrm{perv}}_{\mathrm{obs}})
 =\frac{L^2Q_{\mathrm{perv},\alpha}}{32\sigma^2}
   h^{\kappa+2}.
 \tag{20}
\]
Under independent sampling, likelihood ratios multiply, their logarithms
add, and expectation is linear.  Thus
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(
 (P^{j,h,\mathrm{perv}}_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},
 (P^{0,\mathrm{perv}}_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n}\right)
 =\frac{nL^2Q_{\mathrm{perv},\alpha}}{32\sigma^2}
   h^{\kappa+2}.
 \tag{21}
\]
Replacing (18) by (19) proves the centered isolated formula.

All constants are uniform on \(K\).  Indeed, (4), (6), (7), and (10) bound
\(Z_\alpha,C_\alpha,D_\alpha\) above and away from zero using only
\(\epsilon\) and \(A\); division by
\((\alpha+3)(\alpha+4)\) does the same for both \(Q\)-coefficients.  The
class constants are the fixed values in the proposition.  Finally, when
\(\kappa=3\), \(\alpha=1\) and
\[
 C_1=\int_0^1w\sqrt{1-w^2}\,dw=\frac13,
 \qquad
 Q_{\mathrm{perv},1}=\frac{4(1/3)}{4\cdot5}=\frac1{15}.
\]
Substitution in (21) gives
\(nL^2h^5/(480\sigma^2)\), as claimed.
